body: REQUIRED from the DM-188 review (orchestrator, this run): (1) two-writer run history — a follow-up-run owner may now append experiment events to the SOURCE run's history; if the source machine also appends (status #1 vs results #1,#2) each refuses the other's file forever, and the source machine's next export overwrites the tracked file, dropping the follow-up results (finalizer.ts:657-664 overwrites unconditionally; no resolver/renumber exists). Add the guard: refuse to append to, or export, a non-owned run's history unless the tracked file matches the last sync; detect forks and give a recovery path (e.g. renumber on import when events don't conflict). Demonstrate with two machines (this owner uses a Mac and a Windows PC). (2) A follow-up epic deleted or never shared after a result cites it blocks the source run history on fresh clones forever — degrade to 'cited scorecard not here' instead. (3) Strip correction markers on add_ticket AND every op that sets references at creation (create_epic+add_ticket forged a follow-up that changed a real outcome); meanwhile ignore draft-only holders in other epics when computing landing. (4) Replace scratch/DM-188 c4-reads' timing ratio with a structural test (a scorecard that passes its seal but would fail regrading still reads, or count regrade calls). Pin: unsized-vs-unsized mixes classify; a damaged scorecard holding the breach flips regressed->improved (decide and pin).
